# Pod API — v1.0.0

This document is **the contract**. Clients never hand-write models — they are generated
from this file (`make generate`). If a client needs a field that isn't here, this file
changes first, in its own commit.

## Invariants encoded in this spec

These come from `CLAUDE.md` §2 and are not negotiable at the API layer:

* **No individual streaks.** `Pod.streak_weeks` is pod-level. There is deliberately no
  per-member streak, completion percentage, or count anywhere in this document.
* **The reliability score is never returned.** It exists server-side only, is used for
  matching, and appears in no response schema. Not as a number, not as a band, not as a
  label. See `CLAUDE.md` §6.
* **No shaming vocabulary.** `MemberWeekState` is `posted` / `open` / `resting`. There is
  no `missed`, `failed`, or `broken`. Every human-readable string is resolved by the
  client (or by the push pipeline) from `content/microcopy.json` via a `copy_key` — the
  API returns keys and parameters, never sentences.
* **Proof is ephemeral.** Every `Proof` carries `expires_at`, and the server deletes the
  bytes at cycle end. This is a promise, not a cleanup job.
* **No feed, no follower counts, no public profiles.** Every read is scoped to a pod the
  caller belongs to.

## Milestones

Operations are tagged with `x-milestone`. Everything beyond **M1** is specified but
answers `501` with `code: not_implemented_yet` until its milestone lands.

### `POST /v1/pods/{podId}/continue` — continueCycle

**Say whether you are carrying on after graduation**  
Milestone M6 · Requires a bearer access token.

Answerable only while the pod is `completed` and before `continuation.decide_by`.

A pod carries on when at least two members do — `CLAUDE.md` §6 is explicit that a
working pair beats a forced trio, and that applies to a second cycle as much as to
assembly. Anyone who does not carry on re-enters the pool with no penalty of any
kind: choosing not to do another six weeks is a choice, not a miss.

Answering twice replaces the previous answer while the choice is open.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `podId` | path | yes | string |

Request body: [`ContinueRequest`](#continuerequest)

| Status | Body | |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | [`Pod`](#pod) | The pod, with the choice so far. |

### `POST /v1/slots` — claimSlot

**Open an additional lane with a purchase receipt**  
Milestone M7 · Requires a bearer access token.

Verifies the receipt with the store and records an entitlement. Idempotent by
transaction id: replaying a receipt returns the slot it already opened rather than
opening another.

An additional lane is a second *thing*, with its own goal — not a second pod for
the goal you already named (ADR-026).

## Schemas

### ApiError

The API never returns a sentence. It returns a machine code plus a `copy_key` into
`content/microcopy.json` and the parameters that key interpolates, so display text
has exactly one source and can be checked against the never-shame rule.

`copy_key` always names the **body** string. A client that also wants a title
chooses one locally from `code` — the server does not decide how an error is
framed on a screen it cannot see.

| Field | Type | Required | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | [`ErrorCode`](#errorcode) | yes |  |
| `copy_key` | `string` | yes | Key into `content/microcopy.json`, e.g. `auth.verify.error.codeExpired`. |
| `params` | map<string, `string`> |  | Interpolation values for `copy_key`. |
| `request_id` | `string` | yes | Echoes `X-Request-Id`. Quote this in a bug report. |
| `retry_after_seconds` | `integer` |  | Present on 429. How long to wait. |

### Continuation

Who is carrying on after graduation.

There is no per-member breakdown here, and there must never be one. "Alex is not
continuing" is the most shaming sentence this product could show, and a member id
next to a `false` is one join away from it. The count is enough to render the
screen; the identity is not needed and so is not sent (`CLAUDE.md` §2 rule 1).

| Field | Type | Required | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `continuing` | `integer` | yes | How many members have said they are carrying on. |
| `undecided` | `integer` | yes | How many have not answered yet. Silence is not a no — it holds the pod open until `decide_by` rather than closing it. |
| `you_answered` | `boolean` | yes | Whether *the caller* has answered. The only per-member fact here. |
| `you_are_continuing` | `boolean` |  | The caller's own answer, absent until they give one. |
| `decide_by` | `string(date-time)` | yes | After this, an unanswered pod closes. Closing is the default because holding someone in a pod they did not re-choose is the worse mistake. |

### ContinueRequest

| Field | Type | Required | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `continuing` | `boolean` | yes | Whether the caller wants another cycle with this pod. `false` is an ordinary answer, not a withdrawal — it is recorded and counted, and it is never attributed to them in any response. |

### Cycle

A pod runs for a fixed number of weeks and then finishes. The client is given
counts and an instant, not a week index to do arithmetic on — "two weeks left"
must not be a date calculation on a device in the wrong timezone (`CLAUDE.md` §5).

| Field | Type | Required | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `length_weeks` | `integer` | yes | How long this pod's cycle is. Fixed when the pod forms. |
| `weeks_completed` | `integer` | yes | Weeks of the cycle that have closed. Not weeks the pod *completed* — the two differ and this one is the position in the cycle, not a measure of anybody. |
| `weeks_everyone_was_in` | `integer` | yes | How many weeks of the cycle the **pod** completed — every member in. Not `streak_weeks`, which is the *trailing* run and is reset to zero by any miss. A pod that was fully in for five of six weeks and missed the last one has a streak of zero and five weeks here, and the graduation screen must use this one: the streak would hand a five-of-six pod the copy written for a pod that managed none. Pod-level, like everything else about a cycle. There is no per-member equivalent (`CLAUDE.md` §2 rule 3). |
| `ends_at` | `string(date-time)` | yes | When the last week of the cycle closes, in the pod's zone. |

### Intensity

How much the person can realistically give in a week:

| | roughly |
|---|---|
| 1 | a few minutes |
| 2 | half an hour |
| 3 | an hour or two |
| 4 | half a day |
| 5 | several hours |

The rungs are named for the client under `onboarding.intensity.*` in
`content/microcopy.json`; the numbers here are the matching filter's business and
are never shown to anyone.

The hard filter is ±1 (`CLAUDE.md` §6), so 1 matches {1,2} and 3 matches {2,3,4}.
Someone giving fifteen minutes a week is never podded with someone giving five
hours — that pairing is the one most likely to make the smaller contributor feel
like the weak link. See ADR-005 for why the scale has five points, not three.

Type: `integer` (range 1–5)

### MemberWeekState

`posted` — a proof is in. `open` — the week is still running and they haven't posted
yet. `resting` — the week closed without a proof. There is no `missed` and no
`failed`; the display strings live under `state.member.*` in microcopy.

One of: `posted`, `open`, `resting`

### PodState

`completed` and `dissolved` are not the same event and must never render the same.
A pod that finished its cycle graduated; a pod that dissolved stopped early. Only
the second one carries a reliability consequence, and only for members who were
inactive (ADR-019).

One of: `forming`, `active`, `completed`, `dissolved`

### Recovery

What someone is offered after a pod ends. Both fields describe an **offer**, and
neither carries a reason: the client is never told, and must never imply, that a
pod ended because of anything the person did.

Nothing here exposes the reliability score, the number of pods that have ended, or
any per-member history. See ADR-018.

| Field | Type | Required | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `offer_lower_intensity` | `boolean` | yes | Offer to drop their intensity by one before re-matching. Accepting is an ordinary `putIntent` with a lower value — there is no separate endpoint, because it is not a separate kind of change. |
| `current_intensity` | [`Intensity`](#intensity) |  | What they picked, so the offer can name both rungs without the client deriving one from the other. Present whenever `offer_lower_intensity` is. |
| `suggested_intensity` | [`Intensity`](#intensity) |  | One rung below `current_intensity`. Absent when they are already on the smallest rung, in which case there is nothing smaller to offer. |
| `offer_alternate_path` | `boolean` | yes | Offer the one-to-one path. CLAUDE.md §6: some people need less social pressure, not more. Set after three pods have ended under them; what it opens is not built yet, so the client shows the offer and nothing else. |

### SelfReportReliability

Cold-start only — the answer to "how often do you keep commitments to yourself".
Adjusts the starting reliability by ±0.1 and is never shown back to the user.

One of: `rarely`, `sometimes`, `usually`

### Slot

One lane: its own goal, its own queue ticket, its own pod (ADR-026).

Nothing here says anything about money beyond `entitled`. No price, no provider,
no transaction id, no expiry date — the client renders prices from StoreKit or
Play, and the server needs to know *that* a slot is available, not what it cost
(`CLAUDE.md` §8, data minimisation).

| Field | Type | Required | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | `integer` | yes | `0` is the free one, and is entitled for everybody, forever. |
| `entitled` | `boolean` | yes | Whether this lane may be used. Always true for slot 0, whatever else is or is not true about the account. |
| `has_intent` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `in_pool` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `has_pod` | `boolean` | yes |  |
| `goal_text` | `string` |  | The lane's goal, so a slot list reads as things rather than numbers. |

### SlotList

| Field | Type | Required | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slots` | [`Slot`](#slot)[] | yes |  |
| `max_slots` | `integer` | yes | A structural ceiling above the paywall, unrelated to what anyone paid: someone running this many small things a week is not doing the product in §1 (ADR-026). |
